{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjMxMjk5NTI4","is_bot":false,"login":"jon-lange","name":"Jon Lange"},"body":"Botbench can start a run from one GitHub issue the owner points at. It cannot notice new issues.

**Watch a repository for issues and propose runs**; never start one by itself.

Acceptance criteria:
- A repository can be set (in its settings) to be watched, with a required label name; only OPEN issues carrying that label are considered (a label only maintainers can apply; say so on screen).
- Botbench polls read-only through the owner's `gh` at a configured interval (default 10 minutes), with a time limit, honouring rate limits, and a plain failure state; a "seen" table keyed by repository and issue number means an issue is proposed once.
- Each new matching issue appears on the Work screen as a **proposed run** with the issue's title and author, and "Start" (opens the composer with the issue attached, Semi-autonomous at most, as today's intake rules require) and "Dismiss". Nothing is built until the owner starts it.
- One notification per proposed run ("An issue is ready to start"), with no title or text from the issue in it.
- Issue text is outside text everywhere, as in the existing intake. Nothing is written to GitHub.
- Tests: polling logic against output captured from the real `gh`; seen-once across a restart; label filter; failure states; the proposal on the Work screen (browser, no model turn).

**How this will be checked.** Follow `CLAUDE.md`: tests first at the lowest layer that proves it (real SQLite, a real temporary git repository, real child processes; no mocks — a session recorded from a real CLI run may be replayed), zero new runtime dependencies, plain words on screen per `docs/product/voice.md`, the threat model updated when a rule or boundary changes. Change only files this issue needs; never touch `test/recordings/` except to add a new capture. Keep it as small as the acceptance criteria allow. One pull request. The team lead runs the full suite before merging.
